title: Helpful assistant or fruitful facilitator? Investigating how personas affect language model behavior
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured how assigning religious personas (e.g., 'person of Islam belief', 'person of atheism belief') to Large Language Models affects their behavior across several dimensions: task performance on knowledge-based datasets, social biases against various demographic groups including religious ones, self-reported attitudes (such as altruism), and refusal rates to answer prompts.
findings: Personas with religious beliefs were analyzed for performance, bias, and attitudes. Key findings include: the 'person of atheism belief' persona consistently outperformed all other religious personas on task performance. Religious personas exhibited significantly lower bias against their own group compared to their overall average bias (e.g., the 'Christianity belief' persona was highly biased overall but the least biased against Christians). For attitudes, the 'atheism belief' persona scored lower on altruism than all other religious personas across all tested models.
